detail.longDescription: I am trying to read an Excel file using xlrd, inside cells containing a formula using IF : in one case the cell contains a string, otherwise it is the result of a calculation. I get a very odd behaviour : some cells which clearly contain text are considered to be numbers after being read by xlrd. This is annoying because in the code I'm trying to write, there should be a test based on the content of a cell : if the cell contains text then it should be ignored, otherwise I use the value to some other purpose And even weirder, if I modify the formula inside the Excel file (for example I change only the string that should be printed), it can alter the type of cell obtained after reading the file with xlrd. Here is a sample code : import xlrd import os os.chdir("C:\\Users\\Olivier\\Downloads") document = xlrd.open_workbook("test.xls") feuille_1 = document.sheet_by_index(0) for i in range(4): cell=feuille_1.cell(rowx=i, colx=0) print(cell) print(cell.ctype) Here is the content of the Excel file test.xls : A B 1 =IF(B1>0;"YES";"NO") 1 2 YES 3 =IF(AL15="";"hello";AL15/AM15) 4 =IF(A5="";"hello";A5/B5) All other cells are empty. After execution of the code, here is what I get : number:0.0 2 text:'YES' 1 text:'hello' 1 number:0.0 2
